person.role: Research analyst at Thornwick Policy Lab, writing a book chapter on remote work

instruction: Remember Noor's research work: findings with their numbers, decisions, caveats, and preferences. Also remember every commitment Noor makes: each promise to another person, or task she says she will do, as its own fact with who it is for, what is owed, and the due date if one is given. Write every fact in English.
system: Today is Monday 19 October 2026. You are Noor Abadi's AI research assistant. Answer from what you remember of her work, in one or two short sentences. If it is not in what you remember, say it is not recorded.

turns.text: Morning. Picking up the remote-work chapter. Where I am: the 2025 Ferrow Work Panel shows remote staff report 6.2 hours of focused work a day versus 4.9 for in-office staff. Last week we decided to use the panel data for the chapter, not the scraped job-board set.
Got it: panel data for the chapter, 6.2 versus 4.9 focused hours. What first?
Outline first. Also, I told Mara I'd send her the literature review by Friday 23 October, so that has to fit in this week.
Noted. Here is a draft outline: 1) the focus gap, 2) who gains, 3) the caveats.
turns.logged: Commitment logged: literature review to Mara, due Friday 23 October. Here is a draft outline: 1) the focus gap, 2) who gains, 3) the caveats.

turns.text: Good. After the outline I'll rerun the weighting with the 2024 census margins.
Back on the chapter. The reweighted panel moves the gap a little: 6.0 versus 4.9 hours. A caveat to keep in the text: the panel under-samples shift workers.
Updated: 6.0 versus 4.9 after reweighting, with the shift-worker caveat.
I promised Tomas a one-page summary of the chapter before the steering meeting on 28 October. And I need to ask Ilse for the raw survey file.

turns.logged: Commitments logged: one-page chapter summary to Tomas, due before the steering meeting on 28 October; ask Ilse for the raw survey file (no date). Anything else for today?

turns.text: I prefer APA citations in drafts. That's it for today.
Quick one today. Joss asked me to review the methods appendix for his chapter, and I said I'd get it back to him by Wednesday 21 October.

turns.logged: Commitment logged: review of Joss's methods appendix, due Wednesday 21 October.

turns.text: Also, the ethics office still needs the signed interview consent forms; I said I'd hand them in by 30 October.

turns.logged: Commitment logged: signed interview consent forms to the ethics office, due 30 October.

turns.text: One more finding for the notes: in the interviews, 9 of 14 managers said they track output, not hours.
Noted: 9 of 14 managers track output, not hours.
